title: Hyyve: Shared Memory for Teams and Their AI Agents
excerpt: The landing page for Hyyve, a shared memory layer that turns scattered work into answers people and AI agents can trust. webvise built the launch site and is building the MVP and supporting the launch along the way.
challenge: Hyyve is a new product with a hard story to tell. Most teams already know the answer to a question, but it lives in a Slack thread, inside one tool, or in one person's head. Decisions get re-litigated, knowledge walks out when people leave, and AI agents reply from files nobody approved. Hyyve turns those scattered sources into shared memory that humans and scoped agents can trust, while external systems keep owning the raw content and Hyyve owns the extracted memory. The job was to make that new category legible before the product exists: a launch surface that explains the problem, the memory model, and the trust boundary clearly enough to earn private-preview interest while the MVP is still being built.
solution: webvise built the Hyyve landing page, a dark, architected site that walks a visitor from the problem (your company already knows the answer, it just cannot find it) through how memory is captured, extracted into cards, reviewed, and scoped, to the agent-access model where every agent only sees what it is allowed to. Connected sources like Slack, Linear, Jira, GitHub, Notion, files, and calls stay visible while the memory stays reviewable and every read is audited, and a Request preview funnel captures private-preview interest. The site ships on Next.js 16 with a shared shadcn/ui layer inside a Turborepo monorepo, with the api, auth, and database packages already scaffolded so the same codebase carries straight into the product. webvise is now building the MVP and supporting the launch along the way.
